title: Parabolas as Conics
short: Use focus, directrix and vertex for parabolas opening any way.
trouble: Students forget that p is the distance from the vertex to the focus, not from the focus to the directrix.

blocks.html: In geometry you met the parabola as the set of points equally far from a focus and a directrix. Here we turn that definition into standard forms that open in any of four directions, so you can read the focus and directrix straight from an equation.

With vertex $(h, k)$: $$(x - h)^2 = 4p(y - k) \text{ opens up } (p > 0) \text{ or down } (p < 0);$$ $$(y - k)^2 = 4p(x - h) \text{ opens right } (p > 0) \text{ or left } (p < 0).$$ The focus is $|p|$ units from the vertex, inside the curve; the directrix is $|p|$ units from the vertex on the other side.

Take focus $(0, p)$ and directrix $y = -p$. A point $(x, y)$ is equally far from both when $\sqrt{x^2 + (y - p)^2} = |y + p|$. Square both sides: $$x^2 + y^2 - 2py + p^2 = y^2 + 2py + p^2,$$ which simplifies to $x^2 = 4py$. The vertex, halfway between focus and directrix, is the origin, and shifting it to $(h, k)$ gives the general form.

blocks.name: pre-conic
blocks.cap: Drag $P$ along the parabola: its distance to the focus (red) always equals its distance to the dashed directrix (green).

blocks.title: Vertex at the origin
blocks.q: Find the focus and directrix of $x^2 = 12y$.
steps: Focus $3$ units above the vertex: $(0, 3)$. Directrix $3$ units below: $y = -3$.

blocks.title: Shifted, opening left
blocks.q: Find the vertex, focus and directrix of $(y - 2)^2 = -8(x + 1)$.
steps: Focus: $2$ units left of the vertex, $(-3, 2)$. Directrix: $2$ units right, $x = 1$.

blocks.title: From focus and directrix
blocks.q: Write the parabola with focus $(2, 5)$ and directrix $y = 1$.
steps: The focus is $2$ units above the vertex, so $p = 2$ and the parabola opens up.

blocks.html: Taking $p$ as the distance from the focus to the directrix. That distance is $2|p|$; $p$ is only the distance from the vertex to the focus. In the last example the focus and directrix are $4$ apart, but $p = 2$. Check that your vertex sits exactly halfway between them.
